FOR_QuasitSummon
Shovel is a unique quasit and familiar that can be summoned via the  Find Familiar: Cheeky Quasit spell.
“
Shovel is bored. Shovel wants to MURDERISE.
„
— Shovel

Overview

Unlike regular quasits, Shovel has unique dialogue and can be interacted with after summoning her.[2] Her name can be changed to Fork or Basket through dialogue.

Shovel is a carefree and upbeat fiend that finds joy in murder, arson, and eating babies. She is impatient and very easily bored, but despite her irreverent demeanour, Shovel can be deeply loyal even when denied the pleasures of violence. Shovel is terrified of  sorcerers who do not have the  Draconic Bloodline subclass because she dislikes their "thunder magic and pain". Shovel loves dragons, and a Draconic Bloodline sorcerer and / or dragonborn player character successfully convincing her they are a dragon makes her very excited. She is disappointed if unconvinced, refers to the party member as a "fake dragon", and is no longer afraid.

Summoning and permanently acquiring Shovel

Through the  Scroll of Summon Quasit found in the Apothecary's Cellar, there are several ways a party member may learn to summon her:[3]

  1. The scroll must be cast by a party member with any other class or race besides the ones mentioned above. Then a Warlock, Wizard or Sorcerer[4] must speak with Shovel after completing the dialogue tree below. This spell is not lost upon respeccing. The dialogue tree answers to guarantee the spell:
    • Shovel: So. You're Shovel's master now? Fine.
    • Response: Your name is 'Shovel'? and then with Shovel is fine.
    • Speak to her again to receive the spell to summon her.
    • She always brings up  Necromancy of Thay and closes the dialogue if the talking party member has not interacted with the book yet. After interacting with the book Shovel can be spoken with again, and the dialogue can be completed.[5]
    • The scroll must NOT be cast by party members with the subclasses Storm Sorcery, Wild Magic or Shadow Magic,[6] because this locks the party out of the dialogue tree above. If casting the scroll as a dragonborn, Shovel must NOT be deceived. The other two dialogue choices redirect to the dialogue tree.
  2. The scroll can also be transcribed by wizards, adding  Find Familiar: Cheeky Quasit to the wizard tab in their spellbook. Like all spells transcribed by wizards, it only persists so long as the character has at least one class in wizard. If the character respecs to a different class, they lose access to Shovel until they respec at least one level into the wizard class again.

Alternatively, it is possible to acquire Shovel with any dialogue options if using the scroll in Act Two. This allows to rename Shovel and still get the spell. However it is possible to lose out on some of the dialogue if using this method.[verify]

History

Shovel was owned by the necromancer Ilyn Toth, who was a cruel and neglectful master. He often verbally and physically abused her and forgot to feed her. Despite this, Shovel enjoyed working with her former master.[7]

Combat

Attacks and actions

Similar to other  Find Familiar summons, Shovel excels at providing chip damage and harassment in battle. Defensively, her fragile body is at best a distraction against most enemies. Her invisibility skill is particularly useful for scouting enemy positions and initiating fights via surprise attacks.

Unlike ordinarily summoned quasits, Shovel has her own unique lines when taking actions. Like all familiars, Shovel can drink Elixirs, but increasing her Strength does not help her outside of increasing jump distance since her attacks always use Dexterity.

Notes and references

  1. ↑ Game data erroneously defines Shovel directly as a Fiend rather than a Quasit.
  2. ↑ Shovel is referred to as she in the description of the Steam achievement Rude, Crude, and Full of Attitude: Find and summon the quasit Shovel. Or is her name... Fork? Maybe Basket?
  3. ↑ As of Patch 8, only one character can learn how to summon shovel. If a wizard transcribes this spell, another Warlock, Wizard, or Sorcerer cannot get the "spell-shite" dialogue which grants Shovel as a familiar. Prior to Patch 7, it was possible to learn the spell for two party members by transcribing the scroll on a wizard and then talking to Shovel with another eligible character. This could be accomplished by speaking to Shovel for the second time with a Storm Sorcerer or Wild Sorcerer, with the first conversation happening by the summoner of a different class. Specifically, the first summoner had to be a class other than Storm or Wild Sorcerer, and then carry the conversation through the discussion about the book. Shovel then had to be immediately spoken to again as a Storm or Wild Sorcerer, with Shovel then becoming a permanent spell option.
  4. ↑ There is no minimum class level, but multiclassing may prevent a character from learning the spell permanently.[verify]
  5. ↑ It is not necessary to open the book yet, as long as it has been interacted with and obtained. Neither the order of reading the book nor interacting with the familiar does seem to matter.
  6. ↑ This can be circumvented by having that character cast  Disguise Self prior to using the summoning scroll for the first time. After speaking with Shovel, it is possible to dismiss the disguise and then pass through the magic mirror. The party member can then speak to Shovel again and should be able to learn the spell as described above.[verify]
  7. ↑ Dialogue with Shovel, when spoken to in Apothecary's Cellar
